# How Aurora streams events

Aurora is a small pipeline with three stages. Each stage owns one buffer and hands batches to the next over a bounded channel.

## Stages

| Stage | Owns | Hands off | p95 latency |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|
| **Ingest** | socket reader | raw frames | 0.4ms |
| **Fold** | event → part reducer | parts | 1.8ms |
| **Paint** | layout cache | display list | 4.2ms |

## Data flow

1. The ingest task reads length-prefixed frames from the socket.
2. Frames are decoded into `AgentEvent`s and folded into `Part`s:
   - text deltas append to the last text part
   - tool calls open a new tool part
   - tool results close the matching part by id
3. The paint stage diffs parts against the previous frame and only re-lays out changed blocks.

```rust
pub fn fold(mut parts: Vec<Part>, event: &AgentEvent) -> Vec<Part> {
    match event {
        AgentEvent::TextDelta { text } => push_text(&mut parts, text),
        AgentEvent::ToolCall { id, call } => parts.push(Part::tool(id, call)),
        _ => {}
    }
    parts
}
```

## Why bounded channels

Unbounded channels hide slow consumers until memory runs out. With a bound of `64`, a slow paint stage *pushes back* on fold, which pushes back on ingest, which stops reading the socket. See [the tokio docs](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/sync/mpsc/) for details.

---

**Tip:** run `cargo run --release -- --trace` to print per-stage timings.
